wv_2_toxic_hueco_area.blurb: Toxic Hueco Area is a stretch of the Lower Meadow cliffline in the Meadow River Gorge, part of the wider New River Gorge region of West Virginia. About thirty routes are catalogued here, a little more trad than sport, running from an easy 5.7 up into the 5.13s. Most of the weight sits in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, so it suits strong, experienced climbers more than novices. The wall is known for consistently good rock and climbing, with a famous bolted 5.11d that gives the area its name, a collection of tougher traditional lines, and some demanding sport pitches. The approach follows an ATV track past the turn-off for Tan Wall, then a side path toward the base.
